title: Tenant sandboxing and soft-quarantine policy for noisy-tenant mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several customer incidents surfaced where one tenant's episodic workloads caused multi-tenant degradation on Dedicated pools (high p99 latency, KV cache churn, and eviction storms). We need a containment mechanism that reduces blast radius without requiring rigid hard-slicing that hurts utilization.

Goal: Implement a tenant sandboxing + soft-quarantine policy that detects noisy behavior and applies progressively stronger isolation controls (affinity nudges, batch caps, graceful throughput decay, temporary KV cache limits) with clear audit trails and operator runbook. This should integrate with autoscaling policies and throughput guarantees so we preserve SLOs for protected tenants while minimizing cost uplift for Redwood and customers.
acceptance_criteria: A detection pipeline emits a noisy-tenant signal based on a composite score (latency tail, GPU util variance, KV cache miss spike, token rate burst)

Soft-quarantine actions are executed atomically and reversible: step-1 (throttle batch size + limit concurrent lanes), step-2 (reduce tenant share by 30%), step-3 (evict to isolated lane or dedicated micro-slice)
Protected tenants (tagged via labels/contract) retain throughput guarantees during remediation via priority lanes and autoscale overrides
Audit logs record all sandbox/quarantine transitions and the operator console surfaces an estimated cost/regression impact
End-to-end e2e tests simulate noisy behavior and show that p99 latency for protected tenants improves by >=30% under the same load
implementation_notes: Signal computation: use rolling 60s windows for p95/p99 latency, 30s for GPU util stdev, 120s for KV cache churn. Composite score = weighted sum (p99:0.45, util-stdev:0.25, kv-churn:0.2, req-rate:0.1)
Actions are configured as a policy chain in the scheduler (runtime policy API) to enable atomic application and rollback
Batch size caps implemented via agent-level config flag to reduce continuous batching contributions from noisy jobs
Introduce a 'soft-slice' lane type backed by lower-priority capacity that can be materialized automatically without provisioning new GPUs
Autoscale integration: when soft-quarantine is active for >=2 tenants in a pool, autoscaler evaluates priority-weighted headroom and may provision burst capacity within budget constraints
Telemetry: add new metrics (tenant_quarantine_state, quarantine_score, quarantine_actions_applied) and expose to Console per-route
Cost control: compute estimated RU (resource units) delta per action so billing and cost dashboards can reflect temporary isolation costs
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring function with synthetic noise traces
Integration test: inject KV churn + p99 spikes in staging pool and assert policy transitions fire according to thresholds
Chaos run: schedule 3 noisy tenants concurrently and measure p99 for a protected tenant before/after policy
Load test to ensure soft-slice creation and autoscale interaction does not exceed pool-level safety limits
Security review to ensure audit logs are tamper-evident and no sensitive data is leaked in quarantine metadata
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable detection-only mode on 2 dedicated pools, surface events to Console and Slack ops channel (ops-alerts)
Phase 2 (controlled remediation): enable step-1 actions on canary pools for low-risk tenants (non-SLA) with ops supervision
Phase 3 (priority preserves): enable full policy with autoscale overrides for pools with protected-tenant tagging; monitor cost and SLO metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 4 (global): flip feature flag for all Dedicated pools with default thresholds; provide customer opt-out via contract for legacy tenants
